dublinCore.title: Adaptive Noise and Echo Cancellation
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Adaptive filters
NLMS algorithm
Adaptive noise cancellation
Acoustic echo cancellation
Adaptive equalization
System identification
dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that applies one normalized LMS adaptive filter to three problems: noise cancellation with a reference input (with optional signal leakage), acoustic echo cancellation of a speech-like far-end signal with a near-end talker and an optional freeze during double-talk, and equalization of a +/-1 training sequence through a dispersive channel with before/after eye scatter plots and an optional decision-directed mode. It shows the learned taps against the true path, a convergence curve (noise reduction, ERLE or MSE with the Wiener minimum) and numeric read-outs.

learningObjectives: Apply the NLMS update to noise cancellation, echo cancellation and equalization, identifying the input x, the desired signal d and the useful output in each configuration
Analyze how the step size mu trades convergence speed against steady-state noise reduction, using the misadjustment estimate mu/(2 - mu)
Explain why the filter length must cover the unknown path or channel, by comparing the learned taps with the true path
Evaluate when an adaptive canceller fails: a reference that contains the signal, double-talk during echo cancellation, and decision-directed training from a closed eye
Interpret ERLE, noise reduction, misalignment, mean-squared error, symbol error rate and eye opening as measures of performance
prerequisites: Mean-squared error and the Wiener filter

misconceptions.misconception: A bigger step size is always better because the filter converges faster
misconceptions.correction: NLMS misadjustment grows as mu/(2 - mu), so a large step size converges quickly to a poor steady state
misconceptions.evidence: In noise cancellation mu = 0.5 settles near 9 dB within 200 samples, mu = 0.01 needs about 2,550 samples to reach 10 dB but ends near 27 dB, and mu = 1.5 gives about -2 dB

misconceptions.misconception: Once an echo canceller has converged it stays converged when the near-end person talks
misconceptions.correction: Near-end speech enters the error signal and drives the taps away from the echo path unless adaptation is frozen during double-talk
misconceptions.evidence: Turning on the near-end talker after convergence drops ERLE from about 24 dB to about -9 dB; with Freeze during double-talk it stays near 22 dB

misconceptions.misconception: An equalizer can learn from its own decisions from the very start
misconceptions.correction: Decision-directed adaptation needs an open eye; with a closed eye many decisions are wrong and the filter learns the wrong target
misconceptions.evidence: Decision-directed from Reset leaves the MSE near +3 dB with about half the decisions wrong; after 3,000 training symbols the same mode keeps 0.0% errors

accessibility.screenReaderScript: An NLMS adaptive filter applied to three problems, chosen from a drop-down list: noise cancellation with a reference input, acoustic echo cancellation with a near-end talker, and channel equalization of a plus or minus one training sequence. Scrolling traces or eye-diagram scatter plots show the signals before and after the filter, a stem plot compares the learned taps with the unknown path, and a convergence curve shows noise reduction, ERLE or mean-squared error over time. Sliders set the step size, the filter length, the noise or echo level and the speed.

controls.label: Scenario
controls.description: Chooses the application; loads its default step size, length, level and speed and restarts the run

controls.label: Pause / Run
controls.description: Starts, pauses and resumes the adaptation; the sim opens paused

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Restarts the run from n = 0 with the same random numbers and the current settings

controls.label: Step size mu
controls.description: NLMS step size; defaults 0.05 (noise), 0.50 (echo), 0.10 (equalization); stable for 0 < mu < 2

controls.label: Filter length M
controls.description: Number of adaptive taps; changing it restarts the run. Defaults 16 (noise), 32 (echo), 11 (equalization)

controls.label: Noise level / Echo level / Channel noise
controls.description: Noise cancellation: reference noise rms sigma (0.1 to 2, default 1). Echo cancellation: echo gain g (0.1 to 1, default 0.5). Equalization: channel noise rms sigma (0 to 0.3, default 0.05)

controls.label: Speed
controls.description: Samples (or symbols) processed per animation frame; defaults 8, 24 and 4

controls.label: Signal leaks into reference
controls.description: Noise cancellation only: adds 0.3 s[n] to the reference so the canceller removes part of the signal

controls.label: Near-end talker
controls.description: Echo cancellation only: adds a local speech-like voice to the microphone (double-talk)

controls.label: Freeze during double-talk
controls.description: Echo cancellation only: stops adaptation while the near-end voice is active (an ideal double-talk detector)

controls.label: Decision-directed (no training)
controls.description: Equalization only: adapts toward the sign of the equalizer output instead of the training symbol

visualElements.description: Three scrolling traces (primary or microphone, reference or far-end, canceller output with the ideal output dashed), or two eye scatter plots before and after the equalizer with the eye opening shaded
Stem plot of the learned taps w against the true noise or echo path; for equalization the equalizer taps and the combined channel-equalizer response with the target delay highlighted
Convergence curve of noise reduction, ERLE or MSE in dB with shaded spans where leakage, double-talk or decision-directed mode was on, and the Wiener minimum for equalization
Read-outs: SNR in and out, noise reduction, signal kept, misalignment, ERLE, double-talk and adaptation status, MSE, decision delay, symbol error rates and eye openings

model.description: A normalized LMS filter y = w^T x with error e = d - y. Noise cancellation: d = s + P*x with a 10-tap path P and white reference x. Echo cancellation: d = g H*x + v + near-end speech with a 24-tap echo path H (4-sample delay). Equalization: r = C*a + v with C = [0.31, 0.69, 0.54, -0.31, 0.23] and desired a[n - Delta], where Delta minimizes the Wiener MSE. Signals come from seeded random generators so a reset replays the same run.
equations: w <- w + mu e x / (eps + ||x||^2), eps = 0.05
ERLE = 10 log10(E[d^2] / E[e^2]) on the echo part of d and e
MSE = E[(a[n - Delta] - y)^2]; Wiener minimum J = 1 - p^T R^-1 p
Steady-state excess MSE approx. mu / (2 - mu) times the minimum MSE
algorithms: Wiener equalizer solution by Gauss-Jordan elimination (for the delay and the optimum)
limitations: Read-outs are exponential averages over a few hundred samples, so they fluctuate by a few dB in steady state
The double-talk detector is ideal: it knows exactly when the near-end voice is active

instructionalStrategies: Predict the steady-state noise reduction from the misadjustment formula, then verify
Break each canceller deliberately (leakage, double-talk, decision-directed start) and explain the failure
Compare the learned taps with the true path to connect cancellation to system identification
extensions: Add a practical double-talk detector (for example the Geigel detector) instead of the ideal one
Make the echo path change suddenly to study tracking
